title: Asymmetric queue pressure interaction: root cause and mitigation plan
creator: Asha Patel
summary: On 2026-02-18 we experienced a multi-region disruption triggered by partial capacity loss in us-east-1, which caused traffic to fail over to us-west-2. The admission controller and per-shard queueing semantics produced asymmetric queue pressure across model workers during the failover window. As a result, several per-worker circuit breakers tripped while other workers remained underutilized. Automated load-shedding kicked in prematurely for many tenants, causing sustained SLO breaches (99th percentile tail latency and elevated error rates) for ~42 minutes. This ticket documents the investigation, root cause analysis, short-term mitigations applied during the incident, and a prioritized follow-up plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-18T02:43:12Z - us-east-1 control-plane instances lost connectivity to GPU pool (partial network flap). Monitoring alerted: node loss spike.
2026-02-18T02:45:00Z - Load balancer shifted 34% of routed traffic to us-west-2 per failover policy. Autoscaler began placement but warmup lag observed.
2026-02-18T02:46:40Z - Platform alerts: 99p tail latency exceeded SLO (target <= 350ms, observed 99p ~1800ms). Pager duty fired to oncall SRE team.

2026-02-18T02:48:05Z - Multiple model worker circuit-breakers in us-west-2 tripped within a 30s window. Traffic re-routed back to remaining healthy workers but admission controller continued per-shard queuing.

2026-02-18T02:50:30Z - Automated shedding policy trimmed low-priority routes; customer-facing routes still affected. Oncall applied temporary circuit-breaker hysteresis override to allow more concurrent requests to workers.
2026-02-18T03:12:00Z - KV cache warmup completed for most hot shards; tail latency began trending down.
2026-02-18T03:25:00Z - All circuit-breakers restored and automated shedding disabled. System returned to steady-state traffic routing by 03:35 UTC.
2026-02-18T05:00:00Z - Post-incident internal sync. Preliminary remediation steps documented.
detection: Incident detected by latency alerting on per-route 99th percentile. Secondary signals: elevated 5xx rates (0.2% -> 4.3%), increased queue depth on admission controller metrics, and per-worker CB trips logged in tracing.
impact_metrics: Aggregate token throughput dropped ~27% for duration of incident
Incident duration: ~42 minutes of sustained SLO breach; full recovery to baseline within 2 hours
root_cause: A combination of failover-induced traffic concentration and mismatched admission-controller semantics produced asymmetric queue pressure: during the failover window new sessions were admitted unevenly across per-shard worker pools because the admission controller prioritizes affinity-based placement and local queue limits. Some workers filled their local queues (and saw KV cache cold misses) while others stayed underloaded. The local circuit-breaker logic triggers based on short-window concurrency + tail latency, so several overloaded workers tripped. Circuit-breaker trips triggered re-routing and additional pressure on remaining workers, which in turn increased latency and caused automated load-shedding thresholds to be hit earlier than expected. Contributing factors included incomplete warmup for KV caches after placement, conservative circuit-breaker time windows, and admission policy that did not smooth admits across available capacity during failover transient.
contributing_factors: Admission controller admitted by shard affinity rather than global capacity-aware smoothing
KV cache warmup latency for hot keys increased per-request latency until caches were populated
Circuit-breaker thresholds use short lookback windows and per-worker concurrency counts (did not consider cross-worker headroom)
Automated shedding policies are tied to per-route error thresholds and were configured to act quickly on observed 5xx spikes
Runbook guidance for manual hysteresis override existed but had not been exercised in previous drills
immediate_mitigation_applied: Raised circuit-breaker hysteresis thresholds in us-west-2 for 15 minutes to reduce flip-flop and allow KV caches to warm up (oncall SRE action)
Temporarily disabled lowest-priority shedding rules for enterprise customers to avoid customer-facing outages
Adjusted admission controller to allow short-term global smoothing (toggled feature-flag) so new admits distributed across healthy workers
Expanded tracing capture window for per-worker queue depth and CB events to help postmortem analysis
short_term_fix_plan: Patch admission controller to implement capacity-aware admit smoothing (target rollout runtime-1.22, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2178) - owner: Marcus Li - due: 2026-03-05

Adjust default circuit-breaker lookback and backoff policy to incorporate cluster-level load signals (proposal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/862) - owner: Nadia Gomez - due: 2026-03-10
Add KV cache warmup telemetry and a prewarm path when shifting shards across regions - owner: Rui Chen - due: 2026-03-20
Create an oncall playbook section for hysteresis override with clear runbook steps and escalation matrix - owner: SRE runbook working group - due: 2026-03-08
medium_term_actions: Design and implement global admission controller that uses cluster-wide capacity and permissive smoothing during region failover windows - project: resilience-2026 - owner: Platform Team - target: runtime-1.24
Introduce a cross-worker circuit-breaker aggregator that prevents concentrated CB tripping by rebalancing traffic proactively
Re-evaluate automated shedding thresholds by tenant priority and introduce adaptive thresholds based on recent failover history
Run fault-injection drills that simulate partial region outages and verify admission smoothing + cache warmup paths (quarterly)
Add synthetic checks that simulate cold-KV access patterns after placement to ensure warmup windows are captured in SLO dashboards

verification_criteria: Post-deploy synthetic failover test demonstrates <10% SLO breach window under simulated 30% traffic shift
No more than 2 per-worker circuit-breaker flips during a 5-minute failover window in synthetic tests
Observed KV cache cold-miss latency reduced 75% after prewarm implementation in canary region
Oncall runbook drill completed with <5 minute operator decision time for hysteresis override
postmortem_notes: This incident highlights an important class of emergent behavior where local safety mechanisms (per-worker CBs) interact poorly with localized admission policies during topology changes. The fix is not purely a threshold tweak; it requires admitting with global context and improving cache warmup and observability. We will track progress against short_term_fix_plan and open a cross-team design review to align the admission, serving runtime, and SRE safeguards.
